title: Divergence: forge::check::check_file smears one crate-level verus result across all items — a correct, contract-independent item in a multi-item file is falsely certified L0 with a sibling's counterexample

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content:
Failing tests at forge/tests/divergence_forge.rs::divergence_multi_item_correct_item_not_falsely_failed and ::divergence_multi_item_counterexample_misattributed demonstrate the divergence.

ROOT CAUSE: check::check_file runs verus ONCE on the whole lowered crate, producing a single crate-level VerusResult, then assemble_certificate(item, &verus) copies that same {level, obligations} into EVERY item's certificate. When any item fails verus, ALL items inherit level L0 and the same failed obligation.

REPRO: a 2-item .th file where good (ens result==x+x over body x+x, holds for all inputs) and bad (false ens). forge check reports good as level=L0 with obligation 'postcondition not satisfied @ <bad's lowered span>'. good's contract references nothing in bad.

AUTHORITY:
- thermite-design.md §5.3: 'an edit to f cannot invalidate g's certificate unless g's contract references f's contract.' good is invalidated by bad with no contract dependency.
- thermite-design.md §6: 'The certificate ... lists every function's level' — a correct function must list its own L3 level.
- thermite-design.md §5.1: 'counterexamples, not adjectives' — good's cert carries a concrete witness (a source span) that belongs to bad; a misattributed witness asserts a falsehood.
- goal.md R-SPEC-2 (the certificate is a contract), R-HONEST-3 (a correct item reported as failing is an honesty divergence).

The builder's commit flagged 'per-obligation results are crate-level not per-item' as a schema decision, but this is not additive schema surface — it produces a factually WRONG certificate (correct item reported L0). NOT a blocker only for multi-item-fail mix: the all-pass and single-item cases are correct; the mixed case is wrong.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: PLAN: commit the two failing acto-critic divergence tests at forge/tests/divergence_forge.rs to main as the audit artifact. They are un-#[ignore]d (the dishonest multi-item cert is a release blocker per R-DEFER-3). No production code touched (critic role). The fixer must make check_file produce per-item verus results so a correct item's certificate reflects only its own obligations.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content:
FIXED: forge::check::check_file now certifies PER ITEM (§5.3). check_file no longer runs verus once on the whole lowered crate and smears one VerusResult across every cert. Instead, for each item it builds an isolated sub-program via new fn item_subprogram (the fn + all spec fns as pure shared deps), lowers + runs verus on THAT, and assembles the cert from the item's OWN result. assemble_certificate now receives a per-item VerusResult, so level + obligations + discharged-count are all per-item.

Spec fns (no req/ens/fx contract, §4.2) are verified against the spec-fn set alone (well-formedness via decreases) -> their cert records their own discharged result, never a neighbor fn's counterexample.

VERIFIED green:
- forge/tests/divergence_forge.rs (#41): both tests PASS. good -> L3 with only discharged obligations; bad -> L0 with bad's own counterexample; no smear/misattribution.
- conformance unchanged: sum.th -> spec_sum + sum certs, sum L3 matching conformance/sum.cert.json; binary_search.th L3; broken-contract reported failure + counterexample.
- cargo test -p forge: 25 passed (19 unit + 4 conformance + 2 divergence), 0 failed.
- cargo test --workspace: 0 failed.
- cargo clippy -p forge --all-targets -D warnings: clean. cargo fmt --all --check: clean.

Single file forge/src/check.rs (plus a fmt-only whitespace fix on the critic's test file). No fixtures or test assertions touched (R-CHAR-3).
